title: prefill-decode-stage-overlap-chunked-speculative-kernel-scheduler-kv-cache-optimizations
author: Sana Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency and improve throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads by improving how prefill work is chunked and overlapped with decode, introducing speculative prefill to warm the KV cache for likely next segments, and enhancing the kernel scheduler to prioritize overlapping stages while keeping continuous batching throughput. This PR aggregates a set of related runtime changes that together reduce average tail latency and improve GPU utilization for common RLHF and long-context chat workloads. Summary of changes: 1) Chunked prefill: split long prefill sequences into configurable chunks (default 256 tokens) so prefill GPU kernels can produce partial KV cache earlier and feed overlapping decode stages. 2) Speculative prefill: a best-effort path that computes KV cache for the most probable next chunk(s) in parallel when model confidence is high; results are conditionally merged to main KV if prediction matches. Controlled by feature flag experimental.speculative_prefill with safe fallbacks. 3) Stage overlap engine: pipeline orchestration changes to allow prefill chunk completion to immediately enqueue decode work for ready micro-batches; added backpressure controls to avoid KV thrashing. 4) Kernel scheduler: dynamic kernel selection and a short-tail bias scheduling policy to prioritize short decode tails and speculative chunks to reduce 95th/99th percentile latency. 5) KV cache improvements: lazy consolidation to avoid expensive global merges, incremental KV snapshots for speculative results, and GC tuning to reduce memory churn. 6) Continuous batching adjustments: adaptive batching window that shrinks for low-latency paths and grows for throughput-heavy inflight work.

Benchmarks and validation: included microbenchmarks (benchmark-lab) and internal canary results across p4d and a100 clusters. On our standard chat workload (avg prompt 450 tokens, expected decode 40 tokens): - baseline: p99 latency 760ms, throughput 78 tok/s - this PR: p99 latency 540ms (≈29% improvement), throughput 95 tok/s (≈22% improvement) For long prefill-heavy workloads (prefill 1200 tokens + decode 80 tokens): - baseline: p99 2.8s, throughput 45 tok/s - this PR: p99 1.9s (≈32% improvement), throughput 58 tok/s (≈29% improvement).

Safety: speculative prefill disabled by default for release; enabled in canaries and dedicated perf track. Feature flags and knobs added so customers can opt into stage-overlap optimizations per-deployment. Release notes included at the bottom.

Commit list (high level): "initial chunked prefill framework; add chunker and chunk schedule; speculative prefill optimistic sampler; kernel scheduler short-tail bias; kv cache incremental merge; continuous batching adaptive window; tests and benchmarks; docs and flags".

CI notes: initial CI run had a flaky integration test (runtime/large_context_test) failing under synthetic mem pressure; investigation found race in kv snapshotting when speculative prefills were enabled in test env; added locking and deterministic test toggles; rerun CI green.

Files changed (high level): ["runtime/prefill/chunker.py: new chunker with API to split prefill into chunks and enqueue partial KV results","runtime/prefill/speculative.py: speculative prefill path and confidence sampler; feature-flag guarded","runtime/scheduler/kernel_scheduler.cc: dynamic kernel selection logic and new short-tail priority queue","runtime/kv/kv_snapshot.cc: incremental KV snapshot and merge logic; added lightweight locks","runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cc: adaptive window logic and metrics hooks","benchmarks/benchmark-lab/prefill_decode_endtoend.py: new microbench scenarios and harness configs","docs/flags.md: documented experimental.speculative_prefill and stage_overlap knobs","tests/integration/prefill_stage_overlap_test.cc: new harness for stage overlap flows","observability/metrics/prefill_decode_dashboard.json: dashboard and SLO queries","examples/deployments/prefill-overlap-canary.yaml: example canary config"].

Migration and rollout plan: enable feature flag in internal canary then run perf canary across two Dedicated clusters and narrow set of customers on Dedicated; evaluate at 1 week windows; default off for hosted until additional telemetry filters are in. Rollout controlled by feature flags and autoscale safety gates. Breaking changes: none by default; speculative prefill must be explicitly enabled. Rollback: toggle feature flag; kernel scheduler fallback to previous deterministic path. Release notes: "performance: improve prefill/decode pipeline overlap with chunked and speculative prefill, kernel scheduler, and KV cache optimizations; reduces p99 latency and increases throughput for mixed workloads. Feature is behind feature flags and disabled by default for hosted."
commit_summary: init: chunked prefill framework; add speculative prefill sampler; kernel scheduler short-tail bias; incremental kv snapshot/merge; adaptive continuous batching window; fix kv snapshot race; tests and benchmark harness; docs and flags
review_comments: Jonah Kim: Great direction—can you add more breakdown of GPU SM utilization vs memory stalls for the long prefill workloads? The current p99 gains look promising but we need kernel-level insight.

Sana Patel (author): Added perf traces from nvprof and a small analysis comment in the benchmark script; SM utilization improved ~18% on a100, memory stall time reduced by ~12% for chunked prefill; uploaded trace to benchmark-lab run 2024-11-20.
Priya Desai: Please confirm safe fallback when speculative prefill mispredicts—what's the cost?

Sana Patel: If speculative prefill mispredicts we discard the speculative KV snapshot with minimal copy cost; added microbenchmark showing worst-case extra work is <3% of baseline for our canary configs. Also implemented counters to track speculative rollback rate.
Marco Li: There was a flake in integration tests; the locking change fixes it but make sure locks are fast-path optimized.
Sana Patel: Lock is now a fast-path try-lock with fallback; added unit tests and comment explaining reasoning. CI green after rerun.
benchmarks: chat_standard (avg prompt 450 tokens): baseline p99 760ms -> PR p99 540ms; throughput 78 tok/s -> 95 tok/s
long_prefill (prefill 1200 tokens): baseline p99 2.8s -> PR p99 1.9s; throughput 45 tok/s -> 58 tok/s
speculative_hotpath (enabled): rollback rate 2.3%; worst-case extra work <3%
release_notes: Performance: chunked prefill + speculative prefill + stage overlap + kernel scheduler and KV cache optimizations. Improves p99 latency and throughput for mixed prefill/decode workloads. Experimental feature flags: experimental.speculative_prefill (off by default). Backwards compatible; no breaking changes by default.
